process_area.title: OT Asset Inventory, Architecture & IT/OT Segmentation Governance

value_stream.name: Operational Technology (OT) / ICS Cybersecurity & Retail Technology Asset Protection

fields.Participants: Facilities/IFM (VS-138), DC Ops (VS-04), Store Ops (VS-07), Energy/Solar Ops (VS-108), EV/Locker Ops (VS-163/VS-164), IT Asset Mgmt (VS-99)

workflows.name: OT/ICS Asset Discovery, Inventory & Cyber Risk Taxonomy

Automation Opportunity: - Passive ARP/LLDP/MAC-vendor fingerprinting auto-populating the OT register; fieldbus protocol discovery (BACnet/Modbus/OPC-UA); drift-detection vs IFM/DC asset lists.
Controls: - CTL-800 (ensure controlled execution — OT Asset Inventory, Architecture & IT/OT Segmentation Governance (PA-190.1).)
- operational: asset-inventory completeness extended to OT; segregation of duties on OT criticality assignment; no active scan of a safety PLC without facilities/ops sign-off.
Cross-references: - links to VS-99 (IT asset lifecycle), VS-138 (IFM/BMS), VS-04 (DC WMS devices), VS-108 (solar SCADA), VS-163/VS-164/VS-149 (connected-device channels), VS-08 (POS estate), VS-23 (CCTV/EAS)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Shadow-OT risk**: connected devices (smart lockers VS-164, EV chargers VS-163, SCO VS-149, IoT flood sensors VS-69) procured by business units without security review ship with vendor cloud links and default creds — mitigated by the W5421 onboarding gate and quarterly reconciliation.

- **Discovery-induced-outage risk**: aggressive active scanning crashes a fragile PLC/BMS or trips a fire panel; mitigated by passive-first discovery and ops sign-off before any active probe of a safety system.
System Touchpoints: - OT asset register / OT-CMDB module (distinct from IT CMDB in VS-99); IFM BMS asset list (VS-138); DC WMS device list (VS-04); solar SCADA tag list (VS-108); EV/locker controller inventory (VS-163/VS-164); POS estate register (VS-08).
Time Estimate: - ~3–4 person-days/site initial inventory (~600–800 person-days one-time across 205 sites, phased over 18–24 months); ~0.5 day/site quarterly refresh.

steps.activity: Passive/active-discover OT endpoints per site (ARP/LLDP sweeps, asset tags, vendor manifests from IFM/DC) — never active-scan a safety PLC without ops sign-off.

Classify each asset into the OT taxonomy: BMS/HVAC, fire/life-safety, access control, CCTV/EAS (VS-23), generator/ATS, fuel monitoring, paint/cutting PLC, lumber-yard automation, SCADA solar, EV controller, locker/SCO controller, POS, RF/WMS infra, weighbridge, IoT sensor.
Capture the cyber attributes IT CMDBs miss: firmware/PLC revision, engineering-workstation exposure, default-credential status, serial/fieldbus (Modbus/BACnet/OPC-UA), vendor, safety impact level.
Assign OT criticality tier (Safety-of-life / Store-closing / Revenue / Operational) driving segmentation and monitoring priority.
Load into the OT asset register (separate view from IT CMDB per VS-99) and reconcile against IFM/DC/EV/locker asset lists.

workflows.name: OT Security Architecture, Purdue-Model Zone Design & IT/OT Segmentation

Automation Opportunity: - Firewall-rule / conduit drift detection against the documented allowed-conduit list; segmentation-test automation (controlled reachability probes from IT→OT zones).
Controls: - CTL-800 (ensure controlled execution — OT Asset Inventory, Architecture & IT/OT Segmentation Governance (PA-190.1).)
- operational: IT/OT segregation; architecture documentation; deny-by-default firewall policy with documented exception conduits.
Cross-references: - links to VS-113 (enterprise architecture), VS-27.2 (network/platform), VS-138 (BMS), VS-108 (SCADA), VS-80 (payment network)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Convergence-outage risk**: flat networks where a compromised corporate laptop can reach a fire panel or SCADA controller; mitigated by enforced IT/OT segmentation with deny-by-default policy.

- **Legitimate-conduit-strangulation risk**: over-restrictive segmentation breaks BMS-to-cloud or SCADA-to-utility telemetry and degrades energy/facilities ops; mitigated by documented allowed-conduits and proxy/diode design.
System Touchpoints: - Network segmentation/firewall config (VS-27.2); enterprise architecture repository (VS-113); IFM BMS cloud (VS-138); solar SCADA historian (VS-108); POS payment network (VS-08/VS-80).
Time Estimate: - ~6–8 weeks elapsed reference-architecture setup; ~2–4 weeks per major site/remodel zone design; ~1 week annual review.

steps.activity: Adopt a Purdue Enterprise Reference Architecture / IEC 62443 zone-and-conduit model adapted for retail: Level 0–3 OT (safety/field/control/operations) vs Level 4–5 IT (corporate/internet), with a demilitarized zone (DMZ) between.
Define zone groupings by safety/operational impact: a fire/life-safety zone, a BMS/HVAC zone, a payment zone (POS/SCO/lockers), an energy zone (solar SCADA/EV), a logistics zone (WMS/RF/weighbridge).
Specify the IT/OT boundary controls: one-way data diodes or read-only historians where feasible, application-layer proxies in the DMZ, deny-by-default firewall policy between zones.
Document allowed conduits (which OT system legitimately talks to which IT/cloud system — e.g. BMS→IFM cloud, SCADA→utility) and forbid everything else.
Review at the enterprise-architecture forum (VS-113) and align to the cloud/integration perimeter.

workflows.name: OT Identity, Credential & Role-Based Access Control Governance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-flag of "Eliminate shared/default credentials on OT devices" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-flag of "Quarterly recertify OT access" (replaces manual Step 4).
- System auto-revoke of "Rotate credentials on vendor/contractor offboarding" (replaces manual Step 5).
Controls: - CTL-800 (ensure controlled execution — OT Asset Inventory, Architecture & IT/OT Segmentation Governance (PA-190.1).)
- operational: access control / least privilege extended to OT; privileged-account management; no default credentials on any commissioned OT device.
Cross-references: - links to VS-27.3 (IT identity/PAM), VS-167 (workforce vetting), VS-161 (vendor/TPRM), VS-138 (IFM access)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Default-credential risk**: BMS/fire/PLC devices shipped with vendor-default passwords that are publicly documented — the single most common OT compromise vector; mitigated by mandatory per-device unique creds + PAM vault before commissioning.

- **Standing-vendor-access risk**: a vendor with always-on remote access to a fire panel or SCADA controller is a persistent intrusion path; mitigated by just-in-time, jump-hosted, session-recorded access (W5433).
System Touchpoints: - PAM/privileged-access vault (VS-27.3 extended to OT); identity provider (VS-27); OT RBAC policy on controllers; vendor-management records (VS-161 TPRM).
Time Estimate: - ~8–10 weeks elapsed setup (largely the default-cred remediation sweep across ~205 sites); ~2 weeks per quarterly recert.

steps.activity: Eliminate shared/default credentials on OT devices — per-device unique creds, a privileged-access-management (PAM) vault for the engineering-workstation and admin accounts.
Define OT RBAC roles (read-only operator, maintenance, engineering, vendor-remote) mapped to the zone model (W5418).
Enforce MFA on all interactive OT/admin access; require jump-host (bastion) for any vendor/remote OT session (W5433).
Quarterly recertify OT access — confirm each engineering/vendor account still has a live business need (links to VS-167 vetting and VS-161 TPRM).
Rotate credentials on vendor/contractor offboarding and on role change; revoke standing access in favor of just-in-time.

workflows.name: OT Device Hardening, Secure Configuration Baseline & Change Control

Automation Opportunity: - Configuration drift detection (current config vs baseline); automated baseline-compliance reporting; vendor-visit change detection.
Controls: - CTL-800 (ensure controlled execution — OT Asset Inventory, Architecture & IT/OT Segmentation Governance (PA-190.1).)
- operational: least privilege / hardening; change management; secure configuration; non-prod validation before any live safety-system hardening.
Cross-references: - links to VS-27.1 (change/release mgmt), VS-138 (IFM config), VS-115 (calibration — secure the calibrated device's connected layer), VS-99 (asset config baseline)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hardening-induced-outage risk**: disabling a "legacy" service on a BMS or fire panel can break a safety function or vendor remote support; mitigated by non-prod validation and ops/vendor sign-off.
- **Config-drift risk**: vendors silently re-enable cloud links or default settings during a service visit; mitigated by drift detection and post-visit configuration verification.
System Touchpoints: - Secure-configuration baseline library; change-management system (VS-27.1); OT-CMDB config store (W5417); vendor firmware/PLC revision data.
Time Estimate: - ~2–3 weeks per device-class baseline; ~10–30 min/device hardening in a window; ~1 week annual re-baseline sweep.

steps.activity: Author a secure-configuration baseline per OT device class (disable unused services/ports, enforce logging, disable vendor cloud links unless approved, lock engineering-mode).
Validate each baseline against a non-production instance before deployment (never harden a live safety system untested).
Submit hardening changes through the OT-aware change-control process (VS-27.1) with explicit safety/ops impact assessment and rollback.
Apply the baseline at onboarding (W5421) and on a remediation sweep for in-life devices, in a maintenance window with ops standby.
Re-baseline when a vendor firmware/PLC revision changes; track config drift between audits.

workflows.name: Connected-Retail-Device Onboarding Security Gate (POS, SCO, RF, Locker, EV, BMS)

Automation Opportunity: - PO-gate integration blocking release until the OT security review is recorded; auto-population of the OT register from commissioning data; SBOM ingestion.
Controls: - CTL-800 (ensure controlled execution — OT Asset Inventory, Architecture & IT/OT Segmentation Governance (PA-190.1).)
- operational: asset inventory/onboarding gate; secure configuration; TPRM/vendor security; operational: no connected retail device commissioned without a recorded OT security review.
Cross-references: - links to VS-34 (procurement gate), VS-99 (IT asset onboarding), VS-37 (store commissioning), VS-149/VS-164/VS-163 (connected-device channels), VS-161 (TPRM)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Procurement-end-run risk**: a business unit buys smart-lockers/EV chargers/IoT sensors direct-to-store bypassing the security gate — mitigated by a hard PO-gate block and new-store-commissioning checklist item.
- **EOL-firmware risk**: a low-cost device ships on an unsupported firmware/OS with no vendor patch path; mitigated by the support-lifecycle check in step 1 and TPRM tiering.
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/PO gate (VS-34); OT asset register (W5417); TPRM vendor records (VS-161); secure-config baseline (W5420); monitoring onboarding (W5425); store-commissioning checklist (VS-37).
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 weeks per new device-model review; ~15–30 min/device onboarding verification at install.

steps.activity: Require a pre-procurement OT security review of any new connected device — vendor SBOM, firmware update model, cloud-dependency, default-credential posture, disclosed vulnerabilities/CVE history.
Verify the device passes its class secure-configuration baseline (W5420) and IT/OT segmentation placement (W5418) before PO release.
Confirm default credentials replaced, vendor cloud links explicitly approved or disabled, and logging/monitoring onboarded (W5425) at install.
Register the device in the OT asset register (W5417) with criticality tier and onboarding evidence; block go-live until registered.
Feed device vendor risk into the TPRM tiering (VS-161) and contractual security requirements (SBOM, vuln disclosure, support lifecycle).

fields.Volume: 1 OT firewall/segmentation rulebase per site × ~205 locations (200 stores + 4 DCs + HQ)

workflows.name: OT Network Architecture Review, Firewall Rule & Zone-Boundary Lifecycle

Automation Opportunity: - Rulebase analytics (stale/unused/over-broad rule detection); automated reachability testing; rule-expiry enforcement.
Controls: - CTL-800: IT/OT zone-segmentation enforcement evidence; CTL-800 (OT asset/segmentation rulebase change control); CTL-800 (rulebase documentation retained for audit); operational: every exception rule carries an expiry date and business owner.
Cross-references: - links to VS-27.2 (network/firewall ops), VS-27.1 (change mgmt), VS-113 (architecture review), VS-21.3 (audit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Rule-creep risk**: emergency/temporary firewall rules accumulate and silently widen the IT/OT attack surface; mitigated by quarterly stale-rule cleanup and expiry dates on every exception.

- **Segmentation-bypass risk**: an undocumented modem, vendor VPN, or IoT cellular backhaul (VS-164/VS-163) bypasses the controlled boundary; mitigated by reachability testing and the W5421 onboarding gate.
System Touchpoints: - Firewall/ACL management (VS-27.2 extended to OT); change management (VS-27.1); allowed-conduit register (W5418); architecture repository (VS-113).
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 days/site per review (~205–410 person-days/yr at a rotating ~25%-per-quarter sample with annual full coverage of ~205 sites, field-team assisted); ~1–3 days per change.

steps.activity: Pull the current OT/zone-boundary firewall and ACL rulebase per site and reconcile to the documented allowed-conduit list (W5418).
Flag "any-any" / overly-broad / stale / unused rules and orphaned conduits for cleanup.
Validate segmentation effectiveness with controlled reachability testing (IT→OT, internet→OT, zone→zone).
Approve and apply rule changes through change control (VS-27.1) with documented business justification.
Report zone-boundary hygiene metrics to the architecture forum (VS-113) and audit (VS-21.3).

workflows.name: OT Asset End-of-Life Security, Secure Decommissioning & Cryptographic Erase

Automation Opportunity: - Erase-evidence capture into the asset register; auto-revocation of credentials/access on retirement flag; certificate/key revocation automation.
Controls: - CTL-800 (ensure controlled execution — OT Asset Inventory, Architecture & IT/OT Segmentation Governance (PA-190.1).)
- operational: asset register retirement; secure disposal/erase; data retention — extended to OT; operational: verified erase evidence before any device leaves BuildRight control.
Cross-references: - links to VS-99 (IT asset lifecycle/disposal), VS-59 (store closure), VS-109 (remodel), VS-88 (records), VS-73 (e-waste)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Residual-credential risk**: a retired POS/BMS/SCADA device resold with cached credentials or site logic gives an attacker a blueprint of BuildRight's environment; mitigated by mandatory cryptographic/factory erase with verified evidence.

- **Premature-disconnect risk**: disconnecting a controller before ops has cutover to its replacement can drop a safety/building function; mitigated by sequencing with the refresh/commissioning plan (VS-99/VS-109).
System Touchpoints: - OT asset register retirement (W5417); ITAM disposal (VS-99 W3254); records/retention (VS-88); e-waste/recycling (VS-73).
Time Estimate: - ~20–45 min/device decommissioning (longer for SCADA/BMS historians with data-erase verification); batched at refresh/remodel/closure.

steps.activity: Before physical removal: revoke credentials, close vendor remote access (W5433), and disconnect from the network/zone.
For devices holding data (POS, SCO, BMS historian, SCADA logger, access-control DB): perform cryptographic/logical erase per VS-99 W3254 and verify.
For controller/PLC devices: reset to factory, remove engineering programs, and confirm no residual site-specific logic/config.
Update the OT asset register (W5417) to retired; retain decommissioning evidence per records retention (VS-88, BIR 10-yr).
Coordinate secure disposal/recycling (VS-73/VS-99 W3254 e-waste) so no controller with site logic or credentials is resold or landfilled.

workflows.name: OT Security Posture Dashboard, Criticality Tiering & Risk Acceptance Register

Automation Opportunity: - Posture-metric auto-aggregation from W5417–W5433 feeds; risk-acceptance expiry alerts; GRC integration.
Controls: - CTL-800: ensure controlled execution — OT Asset Inventory, Architecture & IT/OT Segmentation Governance (PA-190.1).) — risk acceptance governance; CTL-46 (posture/coverage evidence; CTL-37 (insurance/underwriter disclosure); operational: every accepted OT cyber risk has a named owner and expiry.
Cross-references: - links to VS-21.2 (ERM), VS-21 (audit), VS-36 (board reporting), VS-26 (cyber-insurance), VS-27.3 (IT security posture)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Silent-acceptance risk**: OT risks deferred indefinitely without an owner/expiry accumulate into an unmanaged exposure; mitigated by mandatory owner + expiry on every accepted risk and quarterly review.

- **Underinsurance risk**: cyber/property insurance under-priced for the OT exposure because underwriter wasn't told the SCADA/BMS/fire-panel attack surface; mitigated by feeding OT posture to underwriting (VS-26).
System Touchpoints: - GRC/risk register (VS-21.2 extended to OT); OT posture dashboard (W5417–W5433 feeds); board reporting (VS-36); cyber-insurance records (VS-26).
Time Estimate: - ~1 week/monthly dashboard cycle; ~1 week/quarterly tiering & risk-acceptance review.

steps.activity: Aggregate OT posture: asset coverage (W5417), segmentation hygiene (W5422), default-cred/baseline compliance (W5419/W5420), open vulnerabilities (W5427), incidents (W5430), third-party access (W5433).
Maintain the OT criticality tiering (Safety-of-life / Store-closing / Revenue / Operational) driving prioritization.
Log accepted OT risks (where remediation is deferred for ops/safety/cost reasons) with owner, expiry, and compensating control.
Feed OT cyber risk into enterprise risk management (VS-21.2), cyber-insurance underwriting (VS-26), and board reporting (VS-36).
Review risk-acceptance expiries and escalate overdue remediation to the architecture/exec forum.
